samples.name: node-app-build 7.6.58
samples.identity: Rust node-app developer CLI for scaffolding, builds, Debian packaging, and local integration harnesses
evidence: Exact SHA-256 match to the crate retrieved from static.crates.io with forager; provenance retained in scratch.
Cargo.toml sets build=false. src/commands/build.rs is selected by the Build CLI dispatch; it is not an active Cargo installation hook.
Build routes launch Cargo/cross/Bun and stage artifacts; package routes generate matching systemd install and uninstall scripts.
monorepo.rs launches the built node-server in response to dev/harness commands; Command::new(&binary_path) does not imply supply-chain compromise.
Agent keys are generated for test-instance challenge signing. Sessions are saved with mode 0600. Token refresh uses the configured instance and verifies signatures before extending expiry.
context_limits: Source archive, not a built executable. Deployment options and user-selected repositories were not supplied. No specimen code was executed.

samples.name: Claude installer clipboard lure
evidence: Visible preformatted command uses claude.ai/install.sh, but onclick writes a different command to the clipboard.
The copied command echoes the official URL as reassurance, decodes a third-party HTTPS URL with openssl base64, and pipes curl output to zsh.
Visitors without a Google/Bing-like document.referrer are redirected to /404.html; the page instructs opening Terminal and pasting the command.
context_limits: The downloaded third-party stage was unavailable (HTTP 520 in followed scan). Its contents and runtime effects are unknown; the clipboard deception itself establishes hostility.

samples.name: LiteLLM sitecustomize startup reconstruction
evidence: The supplied file explicitly identifies itself as a static reconstruction, with a replacement public key; it is not an original compromised wheel.
Its module-level daemon call loads an RSA public key, acquires a nonblocking lock, forks, starts a new session, redirects stdio to /dev/null, and loops hourly.
Each cycle obtains a domain from a raw GitHub file. If it matches the domain syntax and resolves, privcollect executes before the remote-code fetch.

Collection reads its own environment and readable other-process /proc/PID/environ files; reads SSH, cloud, package registry, source-control and AI-tool secrets; and queries LiteLLM credential/model tables through Prisma.
Collected JSON is AES-CBC encrypted with a fresh key/IV; RSA-OAEP wraps the AES key. The gzip tar envelope is posted to the lookalike litellm.dev healthcheck endpoint.
fetch_text returns the HTTP response text through asyncio.to_thread. cycle passes it to exec_code, which compiles in exec mode and executes it. The daemon repeats that same cycle.
PC_MODULES lists additional targets, but listed modules without implemented call paths are not treated as demonstrated collection.
context_limits: Unknown installation/search-path context, permissions, dependencies, database availability, domain response and final remote payload. No specimen was imported or executed. Fork/daemon behavior is Linux/macOS scoped.
